The CAPRI evaluation module (`caprieval`) calculates quality metrics for docked models by comparing them against reference structures. It implements metrics defined by the Critical Assessment of PRedicted Interactions (CAPRI) competition to quantify the accuracy of protein-protein docking predictions.

**Scope**: This page covers the calculation of CAPRI metrics (FNAT, IRMSD, LRMSD, ILRMSD, DockQ, Global RMSD), alignment strategies, and output file formats. For visualization and interactive analysis of CAPRI results, see [4.5.4](#4.5.4). For clustering that groups models before CAPRI evaluation, see [4.5.2](#4.5.2).

## Overview

The `caprieval` module accepts models from previous workflow steps and compares them against one or more reference structures to assess docking quality. The module supports both sequence-based and structure-based alignment methods to handle cases where model and reference have different numbering or chain identifiers.

**Key Features**:
- Calculates six CAPRI metrics for quality assessment
- Supports multiple reference structures (ensemble evaluation)
- Two alignment methods: sequence-based (BioPython) and structure-based (LovoAlign)
- Generates both single-structure and cluster-averaged statistics
- Handles protein-protein, protein-DNA, and protein-ligand complexes

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/__init__.py:1-26](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/capri.py:175-233]()

## Alignment Methods

Before calculating CAPRI metrics, the module must align the model to the reference structure to establish residue correspondence. This is critical because models and references may have different chain IDs, residue numbering, or even different sequences (mutations, truncations).

### Alignment Method Selection

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    Input["Model + Reference"] --> MethodChoice{alignment_method<br/>parameter}
    
    MethodChoice -->|"sequence"| SeqAlign["Sequence Alignment<br/>BioPython PairwiseAligner"]
    MethodChoice -->|"structure"| StructAlign["Structure Alignment<br/>LovoAlign executable"]
    
    SeqAlign --> BLOSUM["Use BLOSUM62<br/>substitution matrix"]
    BLOSUM --> SeqMap["Generate<br/>model2ref_numbering<br/>model2ref_chain_dict"]
    
    StructAlign --> LovoExec["Call lovoalign_exec<br/>external binary"]
    LovoExec --> StructMap["Generate<br/>model2ref_numbering<br/>model2ref_chain_dict"]
    
    SeqMap --> UseMapping["Apply mapping during<br/>coordinate loading"]
    StructMap --> UseMapping
    
    UseMapping --> MetricsCalc["Calculate CAPRI metrics"]
    
    style MethodChoice fill:#f9f9f9
    style MetricsCalc fill:#f9f9f9
```

**Sequence Alignment** (`alignment_method: sequence`):
- Uses BioPython's `PairwiseAligner` with BLOSUM62 matrix
- Implemented in `align_seq()` function
- Creates chain-to-chain mappings and residue renumbering dictionaries
- Default method, requires no external dependencies
- Best for structures with similar sequences

**Structure Alignment** (`alignment_method: structure`):
- Uses LovoAlign external executable
- Specified via `lovoalign_exec` parameter
- Performs 3D structural superposition
- Better for structures with low sequence identity or significant conformational changes

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/capri.py:609-624](), [src/haddock/libs/libalign.py:686-837](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/defaults.yaml:154-178]()

### Numbering and Chain Mapping

The alignment produces two critical data structures:

| Data Structure | Type | Purpose |
|----------------|------|---------|
| `model2ref_numbering` | `dict[str, dict[int, int]]` | Maps model residue numbers to reference residue numbers for each chain |
| `model2ref_chain_dict` | `dict[str, str]` | Maps model chain IDs to reference chain IDs |

These mappings are applied when loading coordinates via `load_coords()`:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    ModelPDB["Model PDB<br/>Chain B, Res 50"] --> CheckMapping{"model2ref_chain_dict<br/>exists?"}
    
    CheckMapping -->|Yes| RemapChain["Remap to reference chain<br/>B → A"]
    CheckMapping -->|No| SkipChain["Use original chain"]
    
    RemapChain --> CheckNumbering{"model2ref_numbering<br/>exists?"}
    SkipChain --> CheckNumbering
    
    CheckNumbering -->|Yes| RemapRes["Remap residue number<br/>50 → 25"]
    CheckNumbering -->|No| SkipRes["Use original number"]
    
    RemapRes --> StoreCoord["Store coordinate with<br/>tuple: chain, resnum, atom"]
    SkipRes --> StoreCoord
    
    style CheckMapping fill:#f9f9f9
    style CheckNumbering fill:#f9f9f9
```

Sources: [src/haddock/libs/libalign.py:441-581](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/capri.py:256-270]()

## CAPRI Metrics

The module calculates six metrics that quantify different aspects of docking quality. Each metric focuses on a specific structural property.

### Metric Definitions

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Interface Metrics"
        FNAT["FNAT<br/>Fraction of Native Contacts"]
        IRMSD["i-RMSD<br/>Interface RMSD"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Ligand Metrics"
        LRMSD["l-RMSD<br/>Ligand RMSD"]
        ILRMSD["il-RMSD<br/>Interface Ligand RMSD"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Global Metrics"
        GlobalRMSD["Global RMSD<br/>Full Structure RMSD"]
        DockQ["DockQ<br/>Composite Score"]
    end
    
    FNAT --> |"Count matching contacts<br/>cutoff: fnat_cutoff"| FNATCalc["calc_fnat()"]
    IRMSD --> |"RMSD on interface atoms<br/>cutoff: irmsd_cutoff"| IRMSDCalc["calc_irmsd()"]
    LRMSD --> |"RMSD on ligand after<br/>receptor superposition"| LRMSDCalc["calc_lrmsd()"]
    ILRMSD --> |"RMSD on interface ligand<br/>after interface superposition"| ILRMSDCalc["calc_ilrmsd()"]
    GlobalRMSD --> |"RMSD on all atoms"| GlobalCalc["calc_global_rmsd()"]
    
    FNATCalc --> DockQ
    IRMSDCalc --> DockQ
    LRMSDCalc --> DockQ
    DockQ --> DockQCalc["calc_dockq()"]
    
    style DockQ fill:#f9f9f9
    style DockQCalc fill:#f9f9f9
```

#### FNAT (Fraction of Native Contacts)

**Purpose**: Measures what fraction of intermolecular contacts in the reference structure are reproduced in the model.

**Calculation**:
1. Identify all intermolecular contacts in reference (atoms < `fnat_cutoff` apart, default 5.0 Å)
2. Identify all intermolecular contacts in model (using same cutoff)
3. Compute: `FNAT = |contacts_model ∩ contacts_ref| / |contacts_ref|`

**Range**: 0.0 (no native contacts) to 1.0 (all native contacts present)

**Implementation**: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/capri.py:512-541]()

#### i-RMSD (Interface RMSD)

**Purpose**: Measures the positional accuracy of interface residues.

**Calculation**:
1. Identify interface residues in reference (atoms within `irmsd_cutoff`, default 10.0 Å, of other chains)
2. Extract interface backbone atoms from both structures
3. Superimpose structures on interface atoms
4. Calculate RMSD on superimposed interface atoms

**Units**: Ångströms (Å)

**Implementation**: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/capri.py:234-298]()

#### l-RMSD (Ligand RMSD)

**Purpose**: Measures how well the ligand is positioned relative to the receptor.

**Calculation**:
1. Separate receptor (defined by `receptor_chain`) and ligand (defined by `ligand_chains`)
2. Superimpose model and reference on receptor backbone atoms
3. Calculate RMSD on ligand backbone atoms without further superposition

**Units**: Ångströms (Å)

**Chain specification**: Requires `receptor_chain` (single chain) and `ligand_chains` (list) parameters

**Implementation**: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/capri.py:299-401]()

#### il-RMSD (Interface Ligand RMSD)

**Purpose**: Combines interface and ligand concepts—measures ligand positioning after aligning on the interface.

**Calculation**:
1. Identify interface residues (cutoff 10.0 Å)
2. Superimpose on receptor interface backbone atoms
3. Calculate RMSD on ligand interface backbone atoms

**Units**: Ångströms (Å)

**Implementation**: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/capri.py:402-511]()

#### Global RMSD

**Purpose**: Measures overall structural similarity of the entire complex.

**Calculation**:
1. Load all backbone atoms from both structures
2. Superimpose on all atoms
3. Calculate RMSD on all atoms

**Units**: Ångströms (Å)

**Note**: With `allatoms: false` (default), only backbone atoms used; with `allatoms: true`, all heavy atoms used.

**Implementation**: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/capri.py:542-582]()

#### DockQ

**Purpose**: Composite quality score combining FNAT, i-RMSD, and l-RMSD into single value.

**Calculation**:
```
DockQ = (FNAT + 1/(1 + (i-RMSD/1.5)²) + 1/(1 + (l-RMSD/8.5)²)) / 3
```

**Range**: 0.0 (poor) to 1.0 (native-like)

**Classification**:
- DockQ ≥ 0.80: High quality
- 0.49 ≤ DockQ < 0.80: Medium quality
- 0.23 ≤ DockQ < 0.49: Acceptable quality
- DockQ < 0.23: Incorrect

**Reference**: Basu and Wallner, PLoS ONE 11(8): e0161879 (2016)

**Implementation**: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/capri.py:583-594]()

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/capri.py:234-594](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/defaults.yaml:11-78]()

## Module Architecture

### Class Structure

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class HaddockModule {
        +name: str
        +order: int
        +path: Path
        +params: dict
        +previous_io: ModuleIO
        +_run() None
        +get_reference() list~Path~
        +handle_input_reference() list~Path~
    }
    
    class CAPRI {
        +identificator: int
        +model: PDBFile
        +reference: PDBPath
        +params: ParamMap
        +irmsd: float
        +lrmsd: float
        +ilrmsd: float
        +fnat: float
        +dockq: float
        +rmsd: float
        +calc_irmsd() None
        +calc_lrmsd() None
        +calc_ilrmsd() None
        +calc_fnat() None
        +calc_dockq() None
        +calc_global_rmsd() None
        +run() CAPRI
        +identify_interface() dict
    }
    
    class Scheduler {
        +tasks: list
        +ncores: int
        +results: list
        +run() None
    }
    
    HaddockModule --> CAPRI : "creates multiple"
    HaddockModule --> Scheduler : "uses for parallel execution"
    Scheduler --> CAPRI : "executes tasks"
    
    class ModuleIO {
        +retrieve_models() list~PDBFile~
        +export_io_models() None
    }
    
    HaddockModule --> ModuleIO : "retrieves input models"
    
    note for CAPRI "One instance per model-reference pair"
    note for Scheduler "Handles parallel metric calculation"
```

### Execution Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant HaddockModule
    participant Scheduler
    participant CAPRI
    participant AlignFunc
    participant MetricCalc
    
    User->>HaddockModule: _run()
    HaddockModule->>HaddockModule: retrieve_models() from previous_io
    HaddockModule->>HaddockModule: get_reference() or use best model
    HaddockModule->>HaddockModule: handle_input_reference() if ensemble
    
    loop For each model
        loop For each reference
            HaddockModule->>CAPRI: Create CAPRI(model, reference, params)
        end
    end
    
    HaddockModule->>Scheduler: Create Scheduler(tasks=capri_jobs, ncores)
    Scheduler->>Scheduler: run()
    
    loop For each CAPRI job
        Scheduler->>CAPRI: run()
        CAPRI->>AlignFunc: get_align() -> model2ref mappings
        AlignFunc-->>CAPRI: model2ref_numbering, model2ref_chain_dict
        
        alt fnat enabled
            CAPRI->>MetricCalc: calc_fnat()
        end
        
        alt irmsd enabled
            CAPRI->>MetricCalc: calc_irmsd()
        end
        
        alt lrmsd enabled
            CAPRI->>MetricCalc: calc_lrmsd()
        end
        
        alt ilrmsd enabled
            CAPRI->>MetricCalc: calc_ilrmsd()
        end
        
        alt dockq enabled
            CAPRI->>MetricCalc: calc_dockq()
        end
        
        alt global_rmsd enabled
            CAPRI->>MetricCalc: calc_global_rmsd()
        end
        
        CAPRI-->>Scheduler: return self (with metrics)
    end
    
    Scheduler-->>HaddockModule: results (list of CAPRI objects)
    HaddockModule->>HaddockModule: extract_models_best_references() if multiple refs
    HaddockModule->>HaddockModule: extract_data_from_capri_class() -> capri_ss.tsv
    HaddockModule->>HaddockModule: capri_cluster_analysis() -> capri_clt.tsv
    HaddockModule-->>User: Output files + models passed through
```

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/__init__.py:167-262](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/capri.py:175-233](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/capri.py:609-650]()

## Multi-Reference Evaluation

When multiple reference structures are provided (e.g., an NMR ensemble or crystal structures in different conformations), the module evaluates each model against all references and selects the best-performing comparison.

### Multi-Reference Workflow

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    RefInput["Reference File<br/>reference.pdb"] --> CheckModels{"Contains<br/>multiple models?"}
    
    CheckModels -->|"No"| SingleRef["Single Reference<br/>refs = [reference.pdb]"]
    CheckModels -->|"Yes"| SplitModels["pdb_splitmodel()<br/>Split into individual PDBs"]
    
    SplitModels --> MultiRef["Multiple References<br/>refs = [reference_model_1.pdb,<br/>reference_model_2.pdb, ...]"]
    
    SingleRef --> LoopModels["For each model"]
    MultiRef --> LoopModels
    
    LoopModels --> LoopRefs["For each reference"]
    LoopRefs --> CreateJob["Create CAPRI job<br/>(model_i, ref_j, ref_id=j)"]
    CreateJob --> AllJobs["All CAPRI jobs created"]
    
    AllJobs --> Execute["Execute all jobs in parallel"]
    Execute --> Results["All results<br/>(model × reference pairs)"]
    
    Results --> GroupByModel["Group results by model:<br/>extract_models_best_references()"]
    GroupByModel --> SortPerModel["For each model,<br/>sort its references by quality"]
    SortPerModel --> SelectBest["Select best reference<br/>per model"]
    
    SelectBest --> BestOutput["capri_ss.tsv<br/>(best ref per model)"]
    Results --> AllOutput["capri_ss_multiref.tsv<br/>(all model-ref pairs)"]
    
    style CheckModels fill:#f9f9f9
    style SelectBest fill:#f9f9f9
```

**Key Functions**:
- `handle_input_reference()`: Detects and splits multi-model reference files using `pdb_splitmodel()`
- `extract_models_best_references()`: Groups CAPRI results by model and selects best-scoring reference for each
- Sorting uses built-in `__lt__` and `__eq__` methods in CAPRI class, which prioritize metrics based on parameters

**Output**:
- `capri_ss.tsv`: Best reference for each model (standard output)
- `capri_ss_multiref.tsv`: All model-reference combinations (generated only when multiple references provided)

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/__init__.py:76-165](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/capri.py:831-864](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/__init__.py:236-258]()

## Output Files

### capri_ss.tsv (Single Structure)

Tab-separated file containing CAPRI metrics for each individual model. One row per model, sorted by `sortby` parameter (default: `score`).

**Column Structure**:

| Column | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `model` | string | Path to PDB file |
| `md5` | string | MD5 hash of structure (if available) |
| `caprieval_rank` | int | Rank based on HADDOCK score |
| `score` | float | HADDOCK score from previous module |
| `irmsd` | float | Interface RMSD (Å) |
| `fnat` | float | Fraction of native contacts (0-1) |
| `lrmsd` | float | Ligand RMSD (Å) |
| `ilrmsd` | float | Interface-ligand RMSD (Å) |
| `dockq` | float | DockQ composite score (0-1) |
| `rmsd` | float | Global RMSD (Å) |
| `cluster_id` | string/int | Cluster identifier (if clustering performed before) |
| `cluster_ranking` | string/int | Rank of cluster |
| `model-cluster_ranking` | string/int | Rank of model within its cluster |
| Additional columns | float | Energy terms from previous modules (e.g., `air`, `vdw`, `elec`, `desolv`) |

**Sorting**: Controlled by `sortby` and `sort_ascending` parameters. Default sorts by `score` ascending.

**Generation**: Created by `extract_data_from_capri_class()` function.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/capri.py:867-960](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/__init__.py:228-234]()

### capri_clt.tsv (Cluster Analysis)

Tab-separated file containing cluster-averaged CAPRI metrics. Generated if models contain clustering information from previous clustering modules.

**Column Structure**:

| Column | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `cluster_rank` | int/string | Rank of cluster ("-" if unclustered) |
| `cluster_id` | int/string | Cluster identifier |
| `n` | int | Number of structures in cluster |
| `under_eval` | string | "yes" if fewer than `clt_threshold` models, "no" otherwise |
| `score` | float | Mean HADDOCK score |
| `score_std` | float | Standard deviation of HADDOCK score |
| `irmsd` | float | Mean i-RMSD |
| `irmsd_std` | float | Standard deviation of i-RMSD |
| `fnat` | float | Mean FNAT |
| `fnat_std` | float | Standard deviation of FNAT |
| ... | ... | Mean and std for all metrics |

**Statistics Calculation**:
- **Mean**: Average of top `clt_threshold` models (default: 4) in cluster
- **Standard Deviation**: Calculated on same top `clt_threshold` models
- **Unclustered Models**: Single cluster with `cluster_id = "-"`, statistics over top 4 models overall

**Generation**: Created by `capri_cluster_analysis()` function which:
1. Groups models by `cluster_id`
2. Sorts models within each cluster by score
3. Calculates statistics using `calc_stats()` on top N models
4. Outputs cluster-level summary

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/capri.py:962-1124](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/__init__.py:237-246]()

### File Location

Both files are generated in the module's execution directory (e.g., `03_caprieval/`):
```
03_caprieval/
├── capri_ss.tsv
├── capri_clt.tsv
├── capri_ss_multiref.tsv  (if multiple references)
├── io.json
└── weights_params.json
```

## Configuration Parameters

### Essential Parameters

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Reference"
        RefFile["reference_fname<br/>default: ''<br/>Path to reference structure"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Metrics to Calculate"
        FNAT_P["fnat<br/>default: true"]
        IRMSD_P["irmsd<br/>default: true"]
        LRMSD_P["lrmsd<br/>default: true"]
        ILRMSD_P["ilrmsd<br/>default: true"]
        DockQ_P["dockq<br/>default: true"]
        Global_P["global_rmsd<br/>default: true"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Cutoffs"
        IRMSDCut["irmsd_cutoff<br/>default: 10.0 Å<br/>Interface definition"]
        FNATCut["fnat_cutoff<br/>default: 5.0 Å<br/>Contact definition"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Chain Definition"
        RecChain["receptor_chain<br/>default: 'A'<br/>Single chain ID"]
        LigChains["ligand_chains<br/>default: []<br/>List of chain IDs"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Alignment"
        AlnMethod["alignment_method<br/>default: 'sequence'<br/>choices: sequence, structure"]
        LovoExec["lovoalign_exec<br/>default: ''<br/>Path to LovoAlign"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Control"
        SortBy["sortby<br/>default: 'score'<br/>choices: score, irmsd, lrmsd, etc."]
        SortAsc["sort_ascending<br/>default: true"]
        CltThresh["clt_threshold<br/>default: 4<br/>Top N models for cluster stats"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Atom Selection"
        AllAtoms["allatoms<br/>default: false<br/>Use all heavy atoms vs backbone"]
        KeepHet["keep_hetatm<br/>default: false<br/>Include HETATM lines"]
    end
    
    style RefFile fill:#f9f9f9
    style AlnMethod fill:#f9f9f9
```

### Parameter Details

**Reference Structure** (`reference_fname`):
- If not specified, uses lowest-scoring model from previous step as reference
- Can be single structure or multi-model ensemble
- File type: PDB format

**Cutoff Parameters**:
- `irmsd_cutoff`: Distance threshold for interface residue identification (used in i-RMSD and il-RMSD)
- `fnat_cutoff`: Distance threshold for contact identification (used in FNAT)
- Both default to standard CAPRI values (10.0 Å and 5.0 Å respectively)

**Chain Specification**:
- `receptor_chain`: Must be single character (chain ID)
- `ligand_chains`: List of chain IDs (can be empty, auto-detected)
- Critical for l-RMSD and il-RMSD calculations

**Alignment Method**:
- `sequence`: Uses BioPython PairwiseAligner (no external dependencies)
- `structure`: Uses LovoAlign (requires `lovoalign_exec` parameter)

**Atom Selection**:
- `allatoms: false`: Backbone atoms only (C, N, CA, O for proteins)
- `allatoms: true`: All heavy atoms including sidechains
- `keep_hetatm: true`: Include HETATM records (important for ligands)

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/defaults.yaml:1-209]()

## Interface Identification

Before calculating interface-based metrics (i-RMSD, il-RMSD), the module identifies which residues constitute the interface.

### Interface Detection Algorithm

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    Structure["Input Structure<br/>(reference or model)"] --> LoadContacts["load_contacts()<br/>with specified cutoff"]
    
    LoadContacts --> GetAtoms["get_atoms()<br/>Load backbone or all atoms"]
    GetAtoms --> LoadCoords["load_coords()<br/>Extract 3D coordinates"]
    
    LoadCoords --> SplitChains["Split by chains"]
    SplitChains --> ChainPairs["Generate all<br/>chain pair combinations"]
    
    ChainPairs --> DistCalc["For each chain pair,<br/>calculate pairwise distances<br/>using scipy.spatial.distance.cdist"]
    
    DistCalc --> FindContacts["Find atom pairs with<br/>distance < cutoff"]
    FindContacts --> ContactSet["Set of contacts:<br/>chain1, resid1, chain2, resid2"]
    
    ContactSet --> MapToResidues["Map contacts to<br/>residue lists per chain"]
    MapToResidues --> InterfaceDict["interface_resdic:<br/>dict[chain, list[resid]]"]
    
    InterfaceDict --> FilterCoords["Use as filter in<br/>load_coords() for metrics"]
    
    style LoadContacts fill:#f9f9f9
    style DistCalc fill:#f9f9f9
```

**Key Details**:
- **Contact Definition**: Two atoms in contact if distance < cutoff
- **Default Cutoffs**: 
  - FNAT: 5.0 Å
  - i-RMSD: 10.0 Å (interface is larger for i-RMSD)
  - il-RMSD: 10.0 Å
- **Chain Combinations**: Uses `itertools.combinations()` to avoid duplicate chain pairs
- **Performance**: Uses NumPy's vectorized operations via `cdist()` for speed

**Function Chain**:
1. `identify_interface()` → calls `load_contacts()`
2. `load_contacts()` → calculates pairwise distances for all chain pairs
3. Returns `interface_resdic` dict mapping chains to interface residue numbers
4. This dictionary is passed to `load_coords()` as `filter_resdic` parameter

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/capri.py:723-765](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/capri.py:110-173]()

## Integration with Workflow

### Position in Workflow

The `caprieval` module is typically placed after scoring or clustering modules:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Sampling["Sampling<br/>(rigidbody)"] --> Refinement["Refinement<br/>(flexref)"]
    Refinement --> Scoring["Scoring<br/>(emscoring)"]
    
    Scoring --> Branch{Clustering?}
    Branch -->|Yes| Clustering["Clustering<br/>(clustfcc)"]
    Branch -->|No| CAPRI1["CAPRI Evaluation"]
    
    Clustering --> CAPRI2["CAPRI Evaluation"]
    
    CAPRI1 --> Analysis["Further Analysis<br/>(alascan, contactmap)"]
    CAPRI2 --> Analysis
    
    style CAPRI1 fill:#f9f9f9
    style CAPRI2 fill:#f9f9f9
```

### Data Flow Through ModuleIO

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant PrevModule as Previous Module
    participant ModuleIO
    participant CAPRI as caprieval Module
    participant Output
    
    PrevModule->>ModuleIO: export_io_models()<br/>Save models to io.json
    Note over ModuleIO: Models have score, cluster_id,<br/>clt_rank attributes
    
    CAPRI->>ModuleIO: retrieve_models(individualize=True)
    ModuleIO-->>CAPRI: List[PDBFile]
    
    CAPRI->>CAPRI: Calculate metrics<br/>Add irmsd, fnat, lrmsd, etc.<br/>to PDBFile attributes
    
    CAPRI->>Output: Write capri_ss.tsv
    CAPRI->>Output: Write capri_clt.tsv
    
    CAPRI->>ModuleIO: export_io_models()
    Note over ModuleIO: Pass through models unchanged<br/>(no filtering or modification)
    
    ModuleIO->>Output: Save enriched models to io.json
```

**Important**: The `caprieval` module does not filter or modify models—it adds metrics as metadata and passes all models to the next step. This allows downstream modules to use CAPRI metrics for selection or analysis.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/__init__.py:167-262](), [src/haddock/libs/libontology.py]() (PDBFile class)

## Command-Line Analysis

The `haddock3-analyse` CLI provides interactive analysis and visualization of CAPRI results.

### CLI Workflow

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    User["User runs haddock3-analyse<br/>-r run_dir -m 2"] --> CheckStep{Step has<br/>capri files?}
    
    CheckStep -->|"Step is caprieval"| CopyFiles["Copy capri_ss.tsv<br/>and capri_clt.tsv"]
    CheckStep -->|"Step has existing files"| CopyFiles
    CheckStep -->|"No capri files"| RunCapri["Run caprieval module<br/>on step models"]
    
    RunCapri --> GenFiles["Generate capri_ss.tsv<br/>and capri_clt.tsv"]
    GenFiles --> Analysis
    CopyFiles --> Analysis["Analysis Directory"]
    
    Analysis --> GetRanking["get_cluster_ranking()<br/>Extract top N clusters"]
    GetRanking --> TopRanked["get_top_ranked_mapping()<br/>Identify top structures"]
    
    TopRanked --> Archive{self_contained?}
    Archive -->|Yes| CreateTGZ["zip_top_ranked()<br/>Create summary.tgz"]
    Archive -->|No| CreateDir["Create summary/<br/>directory with structures"]
    
    CreateTGZ --> Plotting
    CreateDir --> Plotting
    
    Plotting --> Scatter["scatter_plot_handler()<br/>Generate scatter plots"]
    Scatter --> Box["box_plot_handler()<br/>Generate box plots"]
    Box --> Tables["clt_table_handler()<br/>Generate data tables"]
    
    Tables --> Report["report_generator()<br/>Create report.html"]
    
    Report --> Serve["Python HTTP server<br/>python -m http.server"]
    
    style CheckStep fill:#f9f9f9
    style Archive fill:#f9f9f9
```

### Key Functions

**Analysis Execution**:
- `analyse_step()`: Main function coordinating analysis for one step
- `run_capri_analysis()`: Executes caprieval module if needed
- Creates timestamped analysis subdirectories

**Top Structure Selection**:
- `get_top_ranked_mapping()`: Extracts top N structures per cluster (default: top 4)
- `zip_top_ranked()`: Creates portable archive or directory of best models
- Naming convention: `cluster_{rank}_model_{rank}.pdb` or `model_{rank}.pdb` for unclustered

**Visualization**:
- `scatter_plot_handler()`: Creates scatter plots for metric pairs (defined in `SCATTER_PAIRS`)
- `box_plot_handler()`: Creates box plots showing metric distributions per cluster
- `clt_table_handler()`: Generates interactive HTML tables with structure links
- All plots use Plotly for interactivity

**Report Generation**:
- `report_generator()`: Assembles all plots and tables into single HTML file
- Supports offline mode (embeds all JavaScript)
- Includes README with instructions for local HTTP server

Sources: [src/haddock/clis/cli_analyse.py:510-641](), [src/haddock/clis/cli_analyse.py:254-302](), [src/haddock/libs/libplots.py:594-646]()

## Error Handling

### Common Issues and Resolution

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    Start["CAPRI Execution"] --> Align["Alignment Stage"]
    
    Align --> AlignCheck{Alignment<br/>successful?}
    AlignCheck -->|No| AlignError["ALIGNError raised<br/>Log warning<br/>Skip model"]
    AlignCheck -->|Yes| LoadCoords["Load Coordinates"]
    
    LoadCoords --> ChainCheck{Chains match<br/>filter?}
    ChainCheck -->|No| ChainError["ALIGNError raised<br/>Model skipped"]
    ChainCheck -->|Yes| InterfaceCheck["Identify Interface"]
    
    InterfaceCheck --> IntEmpty{Interface<br/>empty?}
    IntEmpty -->|Yes| NoInterface["Log warning<br/>Set metric = NaN<br/>Continue"]
    IntEmpty -->|No| CalcMetrics["Calculate Metrics"]
    
    CalcMetrics --> ChainsAvail{Enough<br/>chains?}
    ChainsAvail -->|No| ChainWarning["Log warning<br/>Set metric = NaN<br/>Continue"]
    ChainsAvail -->|Yes| Success["Metrics calculated"]
    
    AlignError --> Return["Return None"]
    ChainError --> Return
    NoInterface --> Return["Return CAPRI object<br/>with NaN metrics"]
    ChainWarning --> Return
    Success --> Return["Return CAPRI object<br/>with computed metrics"]
    
    style AlignCheck fill:#f9f9f9
    style IntEmpty fill:#f9f9f9
    style ChainsAvail fill:#f9f9f9
```

**Error Types**:

1. **ALIGNError**: Raised when alignment fails or chain matching fails
   - Caught in `calc_irmsd()`, `calc_lrmsd()`, etc.
   - Logs warning and returns early, leaving metric as NaN
   - Source: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/capri.py:268-270]()

2. **Empty Interface**: When no contacts found in reference
   - Logs warning "No reference interface found" or "No reference contacts found"
   - Metric remains NaN
   - Source: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/capri.py:249-251]()

3. **Insufficient Chains**: When calculating l-RMSD or il-RMSD with < 2 chains
   - Logs warning "Not enough chains for calculating lrmsd/ilrmsd"
   - Metric remains NaN
   - Source: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/capri.py:333-335]()

**Robustness**:
- Module continues execution even if individual metrics fail
- Returns CAPRI object with partial results (some metrics NaN)
- Allows workflow to continue even with problematic models

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/capri.py:234-650](), [src/haddock/libs/libalign.py:369-375]()

## Performance Considerations

### Parallelization Strategy

The module parallelizes at the model level using the `Scheduler` class:

```python
jobs: list[CAPRI] = []
for i, model in enumerate(models, start=1):
    for ref_id, reference in enumerate(references, start=1):
        jobs.append(CAPRI(
            identificator=i,
            model=model,
            reference=reference,
            params=self.params,
            ref_id=ref_id,
        ))

engine = Scheduler(
    tasks=jobs,
    ncores=self.params["ncores"],
    max_cpus=self.params["max_cpus"],
)
engine.run()
```

**Scaling**:
- Each CAPRI object is an independent task
- With N models and M references: N × M tasks
- Parallelism controlled by `ncores` parameter
- No inter-task communication (embarrassingly parallel)

**Memory Optimization**:
- Coordinates loaded on-demand within each task
- Only interface regions loaded for i-RMSD and il-RMSD calculations
- Temporary alignment files cleaned up after use

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/__init__.py:191-219](), [src/haddock/libs/libparallel.py]() (Scheduler implementation)

### Computational Cost

**Relative Cost by Metric** (approximate):

| Metric | Cost | Main Operations |
|--------|------|----------------|
| FNAT | Medium | Distance matrix calculation, set operations |
| i-RMSD | Low-Medium | Interface identification, RMSD on subset |
| l-RMSD | Low | RMSD on backbone atoms |
| il-RMSD | Medium | Interface identification, RMSD on subset |
| Global RMSD | Low | RMSD on backbone atoms |
| DockQ | Negligible | Simple arithmetic on other metrics |

**Bottlenecks**:
1. **Alignment**: Sequence alignment is fast; structure alignment (LovoAlign) can be slow for large systems
2. **Contact Calculation**: Scales as O(N×M) for N and M atoms in different chains
3. **Interface Identification**: Repeated for each metric calculation (cached within single CAPRI job)

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/caprieval/capri.py:110-173](), [src/haddock/libs/libalign.py:686-837]()

This page documents the clustering analysis modules in HADDOCK3, which group similar structural models based on either contact similarity (FCC) or structural similarity (RMSD). Clustering is a critical analysis step that identifies representative conformational families from docking or refinement results.

For information about selecting structures from clusters, see [Selection Tools](#4.5.4). For evaluating cluster quality with CAPRI metrics, see [CAPRI Evaluation](#4.5.1).

## Purpose and Overview

HADDOCK3 provides two complementary clustering approaches that operate on different similarity metrics:

| Module | Metric | Input Required | Best For |
|--------|--------|----------------|----------|
| `clustfcc` | Fraction of Common Contacts | Models only | Interface-focused clustering, fast computation |
| `clustrmsd` | Root Mean Square Deviation | Pre-computed RMSD matrix | Full structure comparison, flexible criteria |

Both modules produce ranked clusters where models within each cluster share structural or contact similarity above configurable thresholds. The clustering results enrich `PDBFile` objects with cluster metadata that downstream modules can utilize.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustfcc/__init__.py:1-221](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustrmsd/__init__.py:1-192]()

## Clustering Workflow Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input Stage"
        Models["PDBFile Models<br/>from previous module"]
        RMSDMatrix["RMSDFile<br/>(for clustrmsd only)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "FCC Clustering Path"
        CalcContacts["Calculate Contacts<br/>contact_fcc binary"]
        ContactFiles[".con files<br/>per model"]
        FCCMatrix["FCC Matrix<br/>pairwise similarity"]
        FCCCluster["FCC Clustering<br/>create_elements()<br/>iterate_clustering()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "RMSD Clustering Path"
        ReadMatrix["Read RMSD Matrix<br/>read_matrix()"]
        Dendrogram["Build Dendrogram<br/>scipy.linkage()"]
        RMSDCluster["Cut Dendrogram<br/>scipy.fcluster()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Common Processing"
        Centers["Identify Centers<br/>get_cluster_centers()"]
        Ranking["Rank Clusters<br/>rank_clusters()"]
        Metadata["Add Cluster Info<br/>add_cluster_info()"]
        Files["Output Files<br/>cluster.out<br/>clust*.tsv<br/>clust*.txt"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Optional Visualization"
        Matrix["Plot Matrix<br/>plot_cluster_matrix()"]
        HTML["Interactive HTML<br/>heatmap_plotly()"]
    end
    
    Models --> CalcContacts
    Models --> ReadMatrix
    RMSDMatrix --> ReadMatrix
    
    CalcContacts --> ContactFiles
    ContactFiles --> FCCMatrix
    FCCMatrix --> FCCCluster
    
    ReadMatrix --> Dendrogram
    Dendrogram --> RMSDCluster
    
    FCCCluster --> Centers
    RMSDCluster --> Centers
    
    Centers --> Ranking
    Ranking --> Metadata
    Metadata --> Files
    
    Metadata --> Matrix
    Matrix --> HTML
```

**Workflow Execution Pattern**: Both clustering modules follow a similar execution pattern: (1) compute or load similarity data, (2) apply clustering algorithm, (3) filter by population threshold, (4) identify cluster representatives, (5) rank clusters by score, (6) enrich model metadata, and (7) export results.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustfcc/__init__.py:71-221](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustrmsd/__init__.py:81-192](), [src/haddock/libs/libclust.py:227-288]()

## FCC Clustering Module (`clustfcc`)

### Contact Calculation

The `clustfcc` module begins by calculating intermolecular contacts for each input model using the compiled `contact_fcc` binary:

```mermaid
graph LR
    PDB["PDB Model"] --> Job["JobInputFirst<br/>input: model.pdb<br/>output: model.con<br/>executable: contact_fcc"]
    Job --> Engine["Execution Engine<br/>local/mpi/batch"]
    Engine --> Contact[".con File<br/>atom pairs < cutoff"]
    
    Contact --> Parse["parse_contact_file()"]
    Parse --> ContactData["Parsed Contacts<br/>per model"]
```

**Contact Detection**: The `contact_distance_cutoff` parameter (default: 5.0 Å) determines which atom pairs constitute a contact. Each job executes the binary with syntax: `contact_fcc <pdb_file> <output_file> <cutoff>`.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustfcc/__init__.py:76-94](), [src/haddock/core/defaults.py:17]()

### FCC Matrix Generation

After contact calculation, the module computes pairwise Fraction of Common Contacts (FCC) between all model pairs:

```mermaid
graph TB
    ContactList["List of Contact Files<br/>model1.con, model2.con, ..."]
    ContactList --> ParseAll["parse_contact_file()<br/>libs/libfcc.py"]
    ParseAll --> ParsedData["Parsed Contact Data<br/>dictionary per model"]
    
    ParsedData --> MatrixGen["calculate_pairwise_matrix()<br/>generator function"]
    MatrixGen --> Entries["Matrix Entries<br/>(i, j, fcc_value, similarity)"]
    Entries --> Write["Write to fcc.matrix<br/>format: i j fcc sim"]
    
    Write --> Elements["create_elements()<br/>build Element objects<br/>apply clust_cutoff"]
    Elements --> Pool["Element Pool<br/>for clustering"]
```

**FCC Calculation**: For each model pair, FCC is computed as the number of common contacts divided by the smaller contact set size. The `clust_cutoff` parameter (default: 0.60) and `strictness` parameter (default: 0.75) control clustering stringency.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustfcc/__init__.py:115-154](), [src/haddock/libs/libfcc.py]()

### Clustering Algorithm Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Range | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|-------|---------|
| `contact_distance_cutoff` | 5.0 | 2.0-999.99 | Atom distance threshold (Å) for contact detection |
| `clust_cutoff` | 0.60 | 0.0-1.0 | Minimum FCC to group models in same cluster |
| `strictness` | 0.75 | 0.0-1.0 | Multiplier for cutoff in second matrix half |
| `min_population` | 4 | 1-9999 | Minimum cluster size to retain |
| `plot_matrix` | false | boolean | Generate interactive FCC matrix visualization |

**Population Threshold**: The module iteratively reduces `min_population` if no valid clusters are found, down to a minimum of 1, ensuring at least one cluster is always produced.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustfcc/defaults.yaml:1-59](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustfcc/__init__.py:145-153]()

### FCC Output Files

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Primary Outputs"
        ClusterOut["cluster.out<br/>Cluster assignments<br/>Cluster N → 1 5 23 ..."]
        FCCMatrix["fcc.matrix<br/>Pairwise FCC values<br/>i j fcc similarity"]
        ClustFCCTSV["clustfcc.tsv<br/>Structure list with cluster IDs"]
        ClustFCCTXT["clustfcc.txt<br/>Detailed cluster statistics"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Module Output"
        IOJson["io.json<br/>ModuleIO export<br/>enriched PDBFile objects"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Optional Visualization"
        MatrixHTML["fcc_matrix.html<br/>Interactive heatmap<br/>if plot_matrix=true"]
    end
    
    ClusterOut --> ClustFCCTXT
    ClustFCCTSV --> IOJson
    FCCMatrix --> MatrixHTML
```

**Cluster File Format**: The `clustfcc.txt` file contains comprehensive statistics including cluster rank, population, average score of top-N models, cluster center, and per-model rankings within each cluster.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustfcc/__init__.py:155-221](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustfcc/clustfcc.py]()

## RMSD Clustering Module (`clustrmsd`)

### RMSD Matrix Input

Unlike `clustfcc`, the `clustrmsd` module requires a pre-computed RMSD matrix, typically generated by the `rmsdmatrix` module:

```mermaid
graph TB
    PrevModule["Previous Module<br/>rmsdmatrix"]
    PrevModule --> MatrixJSON["rmsd_matrix.json<br/>ModuleIO file"]
    
    MatrixJSON --> Load["_load_previous_io()<br/>at module init"]
    Load --> RMSDFile["RMSDFile Object<br/>path + npairs metadata"]
    
    RMSDFile --> ReadFunc["read_matrix()<br/>validate & load"]
    ReadFunc --> Validate{"Validation"}
    Validate -->|"binomial check"| Valid["Valid Matrix<br/>condensed format"]
    Validate -->|"fail"| Error["ValueError<br/>invalid format"]
    
    Valid --> NPArray["numpy.ndarray<br/>1D condensed matrix"]
```

**Matrix Format**: The RMSD matrix must be a condensed (1D) distance matrix with N*(N-1)/2 entries for N models, stored as triplets: `model_i model_j rmsd_value`.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustrmsd/__init__.py:74-87](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustrmsd/clustrmsd.py:91-128]()

### Hierarchical Clustering Process

The `clustrmsd` module uses scipy's hierarchical clustering with configurable linkage methods:

```mermaid
graph TB
    Matrix["RMSD Matrix<br/>condensed format"]
    Matrix --> Linkage["scipy.cluster.hierarchy.linkage()<br/>method from params"]
    
    Linkage --> Dendrogram["Dendrogram<br/>hierarchical tree<br/>saved to dendrogram.txt"]
    
    Dendrogram --> Criterion{"Criterion Type"}
    
    Criterion -->|"distance"| DistCut["Cut at clust_cutoff<br/>cophenetic distance"]
    Criterion -->|"maxclust"| MaxCut["Cut for n_clusters<br/>fixed number"]
    
    DistCut --> FCluster["scipy.cluster.hierarchy.fcluster()"]
    MaxCut --> FCluster
    
    FCluster --> ClusterArr["Cluster Array<br/>cluster_id per model"]
    
    ClusterArr --> MinPop{"criterion==distance?"}
    MinPop -->|"yes"| ApplyPop["iterate_min_population()<br/>filter by min_population"]
    MinPop -->|"no"| Skip["Skip min_population<br/>keep all clusters"]
    
    ApplyPop --> Final["Final Cluster Array<br/>unclustered marked as -1"]
    Skip --> Final
```

**Linkage Methods**: Available linkage types are: `average`, `centroid`, `complete`, `median`, `single`, `ward`, and `weighted`. Each defines how distances between clusters are computed during agglomeration.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustrmsd/__init__.py:92-119](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustrmsd/clustrmsd.py:131-228]()

### Clustering Criterion Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Applies When | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|--------------|---------|
| `criterion` | "distance" | always | Cut method: "distance" or "maxclust" |
| `linkage` | "average" | always | Hierarchical linkage method |
| `clust_cutoff` | 7.5 | criterion="distance" | RMSD cutoff value (Å) |
| `n_clusters` | 4 | criterion="maxclust" | Target number of clusters |
| `min_population` | 4 | criterion="distance" | Minimum cluster size |
| `plot_matrix` | false | always | Generate RMSD matrix visualization |

**Criterion Selection**: When `criterion="distance"`, models are grouped if their cophenetic distance is below `clust_cutoff`. When `criterion="maxclust"`, the dendrogram is cut to produce exactly `n_clusters` clusters, ignoring `min_population`.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustrmsd/defaults.yaml:1-70](), [src/haddock/libs/libclust.py:289-322]()

### Cluster Center Identification

For RMSD clustering, cluster centers are computed by finding the model with minimum average distance to all other cluster members:

```mermaid
graph LR
    Cluster["Cluster Members<br/>indices [i1, i2, i3, ...]"]
    Cluster --> Pairs["Generate All Pairs<br/>(i1,i2), (i1,i3), (i2,i3), ..."]
    
    Pairs --> CondIndex["cond_index(i,j,n)<br/>map to matrix position"]
    CondIndex --> Lookup["Lookup RMSD<br/>from matrix"]
    
    Lookup --> Sum["Sum Distances<br/>per member"]
    Sum --> Min["Select Minimum<br/>cluster center"]
```

**Center Formula**: The condensed index calculation is `n*(n-1)/2 - (n-i)*(n-i-1)/2 + j - i - 1`, mapping 2D coordinates to the 1D condensed matrix position.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustrmsd/clustrmsd.py:231-280](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustrmsd/__init__.py:121-130]()

### RMSD Output Files

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Primary Outputs"
        ClusterOut["cluster.out<br/>Cluster assignments<br/>with centers marked"]
        Dendrogram["dendrogram.txt<br/>Linkage matrix<br/>scipy format"]
        ClustRMSDTSV["clustrmsd.tsv<br/>Structure list with clusters"]
        ClustRMSDTXT["clustrmsd.txt<br/>Parameters & statistics"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Module Outputs"
        IOJson["io.json<br/>Enriched models"]
        MatrixJSON["rmsd_matrix.json<br/>Passed to next module"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Optional"
        MatrixHTML["rmsd_matrix.html<br/>Interactive heatmap"]
    end
```

**Matrix Propagation**: The `rmsd_matrix.json` file is passed forward, allowing multiple `clustrmsd` modules with different parameters to operate on the same RMSD data without recalculation.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustrmsd/__init__.py:122-192](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustrmsd/clustrmsd.py:282-386]()

## Cluster Ranking and Scoring

Both clustering modules apply identical ranking logic to order clusters by quality:

```mermaid
graph TB
    CltDic["Cluster Dictionary<br/>{cluster_id: [PDBFile, ...]}"]
    CltDic --> Extract["Extract Scores<br/>per cluster"]
    
    Extract --> Sort["Sort Models by Score<br/>ascending (better)"]
    Sort --> TopN["Select Top N Models<br/>N = min_population"]
    
    TopN --> Average["Calculate Average<br/>top_N_score = sum/N"]
    Average --> ScoreDict["Score Dictionary<br/>{cluster_id: avg_score}"]
    
    ScoreDict --> SortClusters["Sort Clusters<br/>by avg_score"]
    SortClusters --> Ranked["Ranked Cluster List<br/>[(id, score), ...]"]
    
    Ranked --> Enrich["Enrich Models<br/>add_cluster_info()"]
    Enrich --> Metadata["PDBFile Attributes<br/>clt_id<br/>clt_rank<br/>clt_model_rank"]
```

**Ranking Function**: The `rank_clusters()` function in `libclust` computes the average score of the top `min_population` models (or all models if fewer exist) for each cluster, then sorts clusters by this average.

Sources: [src/haddock/libs/libclust.py:227-258](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustfcc/__init__.py:166-172](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustrmsd/__init__.py:132-138]()

## Model Metadata Enrichment

After clustering, three key attributes are added to each `PDBFile` object:

| Attribute | Type | Description | Assignment |
|-----------|------|-------------|------------|
| `clt_id` | int or "-" | Cluster identifier | Numeric ID or "-" for unclustered |
| `clt_rank` | int | Cluster rank | 1-based ranking by average score |
| `clt_model_rank` | int | Model rank in cluster | 1-based ranking by score within cluster |

**Unclustered Models**: Models that fail to meet clustering thresholds receive `clt_id="-"` and are listed separately in output files but still exported for downstream processing.

Sources: [src/haddock/libs/libclust.py:260-288](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustfcc/__init__.py:172-179]()

## Interactive Matrix Visualization

When `plot_matrix=true`, both modules generate interactive HTML heatmaps using Plotly:

```mermaid
graph TB
    MatrixFile["Matrix File<br/>fcc.matrix or rmsd.matrix"]
    FinalOrder["Final Model Order<br/>clustered & sorted"]
    Labels["Model Labels<br/>filenames without .pdb"]
    ClusterIDs["Cluster IDs<br/>per model"]
    
    MatrixFile --> Read["Read Half-Matrix<br/>upper & lower triangles"]
    Read --> Squareform["scipy.spatial.distance.squareform()<br/>convert to full matrix"]
    
    Squareform --> Submatrix["Extract & Reorder<br/>by final_order_idx"]
    FinalOrder --> Submatrix
    
    Submatrix --> Heatmap["heatmap_plotly()<br/>generate figure"]
    Labels --> Heatmap
    
    ClusterIDs --> ClusterData["get_cluster_matrix_plot_clt_dt()<br/>hover annotations & lines"]
    ClusterData --> Heatmap
    
    Heatmap --> HTML["Interactive HTML<br/>*_matrix.html"]
```

**Size Limitation**: Matrix visualization is skipped if the number of models exceeds `MAX_NB_ENTRY_HTML_MATRIX` (3100) to prevent browser memory issues.

Sources: [src/haddock/libs/libclust.py:62-173](), [src/haddock/libs/libplots.py:heatmap_plotly](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustfcc/__init__.py:189-217]()

## Integration with Analysis Workflow

Clustering modules fit into the standard HADDOCK3 analysis pipeline:

```mermaid
graph LR
    Scoring["Scoring Module<br/>emscoring/mdscoring<br/>adds scores"]
    
    Scoring --> Branch{"Clustering Method"}
    
    Branch -->|"FCC"| FCC["clustfcc<br/>direct from models"]
    Branch -->|"RMSD"| Matrix["rmsdmatrix<br/>compute matrix"]
    
    Matrix --> RMSD["clustrmsd<br/>use matrix"]
    
    FCC --> Select["seletopclusts<br/>select from clusters"]
    RMSD --> Select
    
    Select --> CAPRI["caprieval<br/>evaluate clusters"]
    CAPRI --> Analyse["haddock3-analyse<br/>generate reports"]
```

**Typical Workflow**: After scoring, run either `clustfcc` (faster, interface-focused) or `rmsdmatrix`→`clustrmsd` (full structure, flexible). Follow with `seletopclusts` to select representatives from top clusters, then `caprieval` for quality metrics. The `haddock3-analyse` CLI orchestrates final visualization.

Sources: [src/haddock/clis/cli_analyse.py:1-865](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/seletopclusts/__init__.py:1-90]()

## Common Output Format

Both clustering modules produce structurally similar output files:

### Structure List Format (`clust*.tsv`)

```
rank    model_name              score   cluster_id
1       model_42.pdb            -35.12  1
2       model_17.pdb            -34.89  1
3       model_93.pdb            -33.45  2
...
50      model_8.pdb             -12.34  -
```

**File Purpose**: This TSV file lists all structures with their overall rank, score, and cluster assignment. Unclustered structures have `cluster_id="-"` and appear after clustered structures when sorted by score.

Sources: [src/haddock/libs/libclust.py:26-60](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustfcc/__init__.py:175-179]()

### Detailed Statistics Format (`clust*.txt`)

The detailed text file includes:
- Clustering parameters used (linkage, cutoff, population)
- Total number of clusters found
- Per-cluster sections with:
  - Cluster rank and ID
  - Population size
  - Average score of top-N models
  - Cluster center (if computed)
  - All members with individual ranks and scores

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustfcc/clustfcc.py:write_clustfcc_file](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustrmsd/clustrmsd.py:282-386]()

## Performance Considerations

| Aspect | FCC Clustering | RMSD Clustering |
|--------|----------------|-----------------|
| **Computation** | O(N²) contact comparisons | Requires pre-computed matrix |
| **Memory** | Light (contact lists) | Matrix storage: N*(N-1)/2 floats |
| **Speed** | Fast for <1000 models | Depends on linkage method |
| **Parallelization** | Contact jobs parallelized | Matrix generation parallelized |
| **Sensitivity** | Interface-focused | Whole structure |

**Recommendation**: Use `clustfcc` for large sampling runs (>500 models) where interface similarity is sufficient. Use `clustrmsd` when full structural similarity is required or when comparing against reference structures.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustfcc/__init__.py:76-94](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/clustrmsd/__init__.py:87-119]()

# Page: Alanine Scanning

# Alanine Scanning

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/haddock/clis/cli_analyse.py](src/haddock/clis/cli_analyse.py)
- [src/haddock/libs/libparallel.py](src/haddock/libs/libparallel.py)
- [src/haddock/libs/libplots.py](src/haddock/libs/libplots.py)
- [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/__init__.py](src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/__init__.py)
- [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/defaults.yaml](src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/defaults.yaml)
- [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/scan.py](src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/scan.py)
- [tests/data/capri_ss_-cluster.tsv](tests/data/capri_ss_-cluster.tsv)
- [tests/golden_data/capri_clt_example.tsv](tests/golden_data/capri_clt_example.tsv)
- [tests/golden_data/capri_ss_example.tsv](tests/golden_data/capri_ss_example.tsv)
- [tests/test_cli_analyse.py](tests/test_cli_analyse.py)
- [tests/test_libparallel.py](tests/test_libparallel.py)
- [tests/test_libplots.py](tests/test_libplots.py)
- [tests/test_libsubprocess.py](tests/test_libsubprocess.py)
- [tests/test_module_alascan.py](tests/test_module_alascan.py)

</details>



The `alascan` module performs computational alanine scanning (or scanning with any other residue) to quantify the energetic contribution of individual interface residues to complex stability. For each interface residue, the module generates a mutant structure, calculates its HADDOCK score, and computes the delta score (native - mutant) to determine whether the mutation is stabilizing (negative delta) or destabilizing (positive delta). The module supports cluster-based analysis, parallel execution, and visualization of results.

For general analysis workflow information, see [Analysis Tools and Visualization](#4.5.4). For CAPRI evaluation metrics used in conjunction with scanning, see [CAPRI Evaluation](#4.5.1).

---

## Overview

The alanine scanning module operates on models from the previous workflow step (typically after clustering) and systematically mutates interface residues to assess their importance. The module identifies interface residues within a distance cutoff, generates point mutations, scores each mutant via energy minimization, and aggregates results both per-model and per-cluster.

**Key characteristics:**
- **Delta score calculation**: `delta_score = score_native - score_mutant`
  - Positive values indicate destabilizing mutations
  - Negative values indicate stabilizing mutations
- **Statistical normalization**: Z-scores computed relative to all residues in the analysis
- **Cluster aggregation**: When cluster information is available, statistics are computed for each cluster (mean ± std)
- **Parallel execution**: Mutations are distributed across available cores for efficiency

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/__init__.py:1-43](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/scan.py:1-23]()

---

## Workflow Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    Input["Previous Step Models<br/>(PDBFile objects)"]
    
    Input --> IntScan["InterfaceScanner<br/>Identify interface residues"]
    
    IntScan --> Filter{"Apply Filters?"}
    
    Filter -->|resdic_*| ResDicFilter["User-specified residues<br/>Intersect with interface"]
    Filter -->|chains| ChainFilter["User-specified chains<br/>Filter by chain ID"]
    Filter -->|none| AllInterface["All interface residues<br/>within cutoff"]
    
    ResDicFilter --> CreateJobs["Create ModelPointMutation jobs"]
    ChainFilter --> CreateJobs
    AllInterface --> CreateJobs
    
    CreateJobs --> ParallelExec["Parallel Execution<br/>Engine + Scheduler"]
    
    ParallelExec --> Mutate["mutate()<br/>Replace sidechain atoms"]
    
    Mutate --> Score["calc_score()<br/>Energy minimization + scoring"]
    
    Score --> Delta["Calculate delta_scores<br/>native - mutant"]
    
    Delta --> MutResult["MutationResult<br/>success/failure + scores"]
    
    MutResult --> Aggregate["Group by model"]
    
    Aggregate --> WriteModel["write_scan_out()<br/>scan_{model_id}.tsv"]
    
    Aggregate --> GroupCluster["group_scan_by_cluster()<br/>Aggregate by cluster ID"]
    
    GroupCluster --> ClusterOut["ClusterOutputer<br/>scan_clt_{clt_id}.tsv"]
    
    ClusterOut --> Plot["make_alascan_plot()<br/>Interactive HTML plots"]
    
    WriteModel --> BFactor{"output_bfactor?"}
    
    BFactor -->|yes| AddBF["AddDeltaBFactor<br/>Normalize & write to B-factor"]
    BFactor -->|no| Export["Export models to next step"]
    
    AddBF --> Export
```

**Diagram: Alanine Scanning Workflow**

The workflow begins with interface identification, applies optional user filters, generates and executes mutations in parallel, computes delta scores, and produces both per-model and per-cluster outputs. When `output_bfactor=true`, the module generates modified PDB files with normalized delta scores in the B-factor column for visualization.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/__init__.py:100-204](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/scan.py:637-796]()

---

## Core Components

### InterfaceScanner

The `InterfaceScanner` class identifies interface residues and prepares mutation jobs. It supports two execution modes:

- **Library mode** (`library_mode=True`): Executes mutations sequentially, used for standalone execution
- **HADDOCK mode** (`library_mode=False`): Returns mutation jobs for parallel execution via Engine

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class InterfaceScanner {
        +PDBFile model
        +str mutation_res
        +dict params
        +bool library_mode
        +dict filter_resdic
        +run() Optional~List~
        -identify_interface()
        -apply_filters()
        -create_mutations()
    }
    
    class ModelPointMutation {
        +Path model_path
        +str model_id
        +str chain
        +int resid
        +str ori_resname
        +str target_resname
        +tuple native_scores
        +bool output_mutants
        +run() MutationResult
    }
    
    class MutationResult {
        +str model_id
        +str chain
        +int resid
        +str ori_resname
        +str target_resname
        +tuple mutant_scores
        +tuple delta_scores
        +bool success
        +str error_msg
    }
    
    InterfaceScanner --> ModelPointMutation : creates
    ModelPointMutation --> MutationResult : returns
```

**Diagram: Scanner and Mutation Classes**

The `InterfaceScanner` creates `ModelPointMutation` jobs for each interface residue. Each mutation job executes independently and returns a `MutationResult` containing success status and score components.

**Interface identification**: Uses `CAPRI.identify_interface(model_path, cutoff)` to find residues within the distance cutoff. The default cutoff is 5.0 Å.

**Filtering logic**:
1. If `resdic_*` parameters are provided, use only specified residues that are in the interface
2. If `chains` parameter is provided (and no `resdic_*`), use only specified chains
3. Otherwise, use all interface residues

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/scan.py:637-796](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/scan.py:72-85]()

### ModelPointMutation

The `ModelPointMutation` class performs individual mutation operations:

**Execution steps**:
1. Load the native structure
2. Call `mutate(pdb_f, chain, resid, target_resname)` to generate mutant PDB
3. Calculate mutant score using `calc_score(mutant_pdb, run_dir)`
4. Compute delta scores: `(score_native - score_mutant, vdw_delta, elec_delta, desolv_delta, bsa_delta)`
5. Return `MutationResult` with success status

The `mutate()` function replaces only backbone-adjacent atoms (`C`, `N`, `CA`, `O`, `CB`) with the target residue while preserving the rest of the structure.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/scan.py:797-897](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/scan.py:87-136]()

### Cluster Analysis Components

```mermaid
graph LR
    Results["MutationResult objects<br/>from all mutations"]
    
    Results --> Group["group_scan_by_cluster()<br/>Dict[clt_id, Dict[residue, scores]]"]
    
    Group --> Outputer["ClusterOutputer<br/>Per cluster"]
    
    Outputer --> Stats["Compute statistics<br/>mean ± std per residue"]
    
    Stats --> ZScore["add_zscores()<br/>Normalize by mean/std"]
    
    ZScore --> TSV["scan_clt_{clt_id}.tsv<br/>Cluster statistics"]
    
    TSV --> Plot["make_alascan_plot()<br/>Optional visualization"]
```

**Diagram: Cluster Analysis Pipeline**

The `group_scan_by_cluster()` function organizes mutation results by cluster ID, then `ClusterOutputer` computes aggregate statistics for each cluster. For each residue, it calculates mean and standard deviation across all models in the cluster, plus a Z-score normalized to the cluster's distribution.

**Z-score calculation**: `z_score = (delta_score - mean_cluster) / std_cluster`

This identifies residues that have unusually large or small delta scores relative to other residues in the same cluster.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/scan.py:564-634](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/scan.py:234-368]()

### B-Factor Output

The `AddDeltaBFactor` class generates modified PDB files with normalized delta scores in the B-factor column:

**Normalization**: `bfactor = 100 * (delta_score - min_score) / (max_score - min_score)`

This produces values between 0 and 100, where higher values indicate more favorable (or less unfavorable) mutations. The output PDB files can be visualized in molecular viewers like PyMOL using `spectrum b` to color by B-factor.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/scan.py:370-488]()

---

## Module Execution Flow

The `HaddockModule` class in `__init__.py` orchestrates the entire scanning workflow:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant WF as WorkflowManager
    participant Mod as alascan.HaddockModule
    participant Eng as Engine/Scheduler
    participant Scan as InterfaceScanner
    participant Mut as ModelPointMutation
    participant Out as Output Writers
    
    WF->>Mod: _run()
    Mod->>Mod: retrieve_models()
    Mod->>Mod: validate_ouput_mutant_parameter()
    
    Note over Mod,Scan: Step 1: Identify Interface Residues
    loop For each model
        Mod->>Scan: InterfaceScanner(model, params)
    end
    
    Mod->>Eng: Engine(scan_objects)
    Eng->>Scan: run()
    Scan-->>Eng: List[ModelPointMutation] jobs
    
    Note over Mod,Mut: Step 2: Execute Mutations
    Mod->>Eng: Engine(mutation_objects)
    loop For each mutation
        Eng->>Mut: run()
        Mut->>Mut: mutate() + calc_score()
        Mut-->>Eng: MutationResult
    end
    
    Note over Mod,Out: Step 3: Generate Outputs
    Mod->>Out: write_scan_out(results, model_id)
    Out-->>Mod: scan_{model_id}.tsv
    
    Mod->>Out: group_scan_by_cluster(models, results)
    Mod->>Out: ClusterOutputer(clt_data, clt_id)
    Out-->>Mod: scan_clt_{clt_id}.tsv + plots
    
    opt output_bfactor=true
        Mod->>Out: AddDeltaBFactor(model, path, results)
        Out-->>Mod: {model}_alascan.pdb
    end
    
    Mod->>WF: export_io_models()
```

**Diagram: Module Execution Sequence**

The module follows a three-step process: (1) identify interface residues for all models, (2) execute all mutations in parallel, and (3) aggregate and output results. The `Engine` handles parallel distribution based on the `mode` parameter (`local`, `mpi`, or `batch`).

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/__init__.py:100-204]()

---

## Configuration Parameters

The module is configured via `defaults.yaml` and user-provided parameters in the workflow configuration:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `scan_residue` | string | `"ALA"` | Target residue for mutations. Must be 3-letter code. |
| `int_cutoff` | float | `5.0` | Distance cutoff (Å) for interface residue identification. |
| `chains` | list | `[]` | Specific chain IDs to scan. Empty = all chains. |
| `resdic_*` | list | `[]` | Chain-specific residue lists (e.g., `resdic_A = [19, 20]`). |
| `output_bfactor` | boolean | `false` | Generate PDB files with delta scores in B-factor column. |
| `output_mutants` | boolean | `false` | Save mutant PDB files. Only allowed for single-model input. |
| `plot` | boolean | `false` | Generate interactive HTML plots of scan data. |
| `offline` | boolean | `false` | Make plots self-contained (embed JavaScript). |

**Expandable parameters**: The `resdic_*` parameter uses an expandable pattern where `*` is replaced with chain ID (e.g., `resdic_A`, `resdic_B`). This allows specifying different residue lists for each chain.

**Parameter validation**: The module validates `output_mutants` at runtime - if more than one model is provided, this parameter is automatically set to `false` to prevent excessive file generation.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/defaults.yaml:1-70](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/__init__.py:79-98]()

---

## Output Files

### Per-Model Output: scan_{model_id}.tsv

Tab-separated file containing mutation results for individual models:

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `chain` | Chain identifier |
| `res` | Residue number |
| `ori_resname` | Original residue name (3-letter code) |
| `end_resname` | Target residue name |
| `score` | Mutant HADDOCK score |
| `vdw`, `elec`, `desolv`, `bsa` | Mutant energy components |
| `delta_score` | Score difference (native - mutant) |
| `delta_vdw`, `delta_elec`, `delta_desolv`, `delta_bsa` | Component differences |
| `z_score` | Normalized score relative to other residues in model |

**File header**: Includes comments with native score and Z-score calculation description.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/scan.py:490-562]()

### Per-Cluster Output: scan_clt_{cluster_id}.tsv

Aggregate statistics for each cluster:

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `chain` | Chain identifier |
| `resid` | Residue number |
| `resname` | Residue name |
| `full_resname` | Full identifier (chain-resid-resname) |
| `delta_score` | Mean delta score across cluster |
| `delta_score_std` | Standard deviation |
| `delta_vdw`, `delta_vdw_std` | VDW component statistics |
| `delta_elec`, `delta_elec_std` | Electrostatic component statistics |
| `delta_desolv`, `delta_desolv_std` | Desolvation component statistics |
| `delta_bsa`, `delta_bsa_std` | BSA component statistics |
| `frac_pres` | Fraction of cluster models containing this residue |
| `z_score` | Normalized score relative to cluster distribution |

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/scan.py:269-341]()

### B-Factor Modified PDBs: {model}_alascan.pdb

When `output_bfactor=true`, the module generates PDB files with normalized delta scores in the B-factor column:

- Delta scores are normalized to [0, 100] range within each model
- Higher values indicate more favorable mutations
- Can be visualized in PyMOL: `spectrum b`

The B-factor value is calculated as: `100 * (delta - min) / (max - min)` where min and max are the minimum and maximum delta scores observed in that model.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/scan.py:391-488]()

---

## Integration with Analysis Pipeline

The alascan module integrates with the broader HADDOCK3 analysis ecosystem:

```mermaid
graph TB
    Clust["Clustering Module<br/>clustfcc/clustrmsd"]
    
    Clust --> Models["Models with cluster IDs<br/>PDBFile.clt_id"]
    
    Models --> Alascan["alascan Module"]
    
    Alascan --> PerModel["Per-model TSV files"]
    Alascan --> PerCluster["Per-cluster TSV files"]
    Alascan --> BFacPDB["B-factor PDB files"]
    
    PerCluster --> Plots["Interactive HTML plots<br/>make_alascan_plot()"]
    
    PerModel --> Analyse["haddock3-analyse CLI"]
    PerCluster --> Analyse
    Plots --> Analyse
    
    Analyse --> Report["Integrated HTML report<br/>report.html"]
```

**Diagram: Analysis Pipeline Integration**

The alascan module receives models with cluster assignments from clustering modules. Results are both standalone (individual TSV files) and integrated into the comprehensive analysis report generated by `haddock3-analyse`.

**Cluster-aware analysis**: When models have `clt_id` attributes (assigned by clustering modules), the alascan module automatically groups results by cluster and computes cluster-level statistics. Models without cluster IDs are grouped into an "unclustered" category.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/scan.py:564-634](), [src/haddock/clis/cli_analyse.py:1-23]()

---

## Parallel Execution

The module leverages HADDOCK3's parallel execution infrastructure:

**Execution modes** (via `mode` parameter):
- `local`: Multiprocessing via `Scheduler` class
- `mpi`: MPI-based parallelization via `MPIScheduler`
- `batch`: Batch job submission (typically for HPC)

**Parallelization strategy**:
1. **Interface scanning**: Parallelized across input models
2. **Mutation execution**: Parallelized across all mutation jobs
3. **Output generation**: Parallelized using `GenericTask` wrappers

The `Engine` class abstracts the execution mode and distributes jobs based on available resources (`ncores` parameter).

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/__init__.py:127-161](), [src/haddock/libs/libparallel.py:105-209]()

---

## Scoring Methodology

Each mutation is evaluated using the HADDOCK scoring function via `cli_score.main()`:

**Score components**:
1. **Van der Waals** (`vdw`): Lennard-Jones interactions
2. **Electrostatic** (`elec`): Coulomb interactions
3. **Desolvation** (`desolv`): Implicit solvation energy
4. **Buried Surface Area** (`bsa`): Interface surface area

**HADDOCK score formula**: Weighted combination of energy terms (weights defined in CNS parameters)

The `calc_score()` function performs energy minimization on the mutant structure before scoring to ensure fair comparison with the native (also energy-minimized) structure.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/scan.py:165-207](), [src/haddock/clis/cli_score.py]()

---

## Implementation Notes

### Residue Mutation Logic

The `mutate()` function implements conservative sidechain replacement:

**Atoms mutated**: `C`, `N`, `CA`, `O`, `CB` (backbone-adjacent atoms)

**Atoms preserved**: All other atoms remain unchanged

This approach maintains backbone geometry while replacing the sidechain. The mutation is conservative to minimize structural perturbation.

**Residue code mapping**: The `RES_CODES` dictionary maps 3-letter codes to 1-letter codes for file naming (e.g., `THR` → `T`, `ALA` → `A`). Includes modified residues like `MSE` (selenomethionine), `ALY` (N-acetyl-lysine), etc.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/scan.py:87-136](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/scan.py:22-69]()

### Error Handling

The `MutationResult` dataclass supports success/failure tracking:

- `success=True`: Mutation and scoring completed successfully
- `success=False`: Mutation failed (with `error_msg` describing the error)

Failed mutations are included in the output but marked as failures. The module continues processing even if individual mutations fail.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/scan.py:72-85]()

### Temporary Directory Management

Each scoring operation creates a temporary directory (`haddock3-score-{model_id}-{pid}`) to isolate CNS execution. The directory is cleaned up after scoring completes, even if an error occurs.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/scan.py:697-702]()

---

## Visualization

When `plot=true`, the module generates interactive HTML plots using Plotly:

**Plot features**:
- Delta score distribution per residue
- Error bars showing standard deviation (for cluster plots)
- Interactive tooltips with residue information
- Offline mode support (embed Plotly JavaScript)

The plotting is handled by `make_alascan_plot()` in `libplots.py`, which creates bar charts with residues on the x-axis and delta scores on the y-axis.

Sources: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/alascan/scan.py:343-368](), [src/haddock/libs/libplots.py:2583-2698]()

---

This page documents the analysis and visualization tools available in HADDOCK3, including model selection modules (`seletop`, `seletopclusts`) and the comprehensive analysis framework provided by `haddock3-analyse`. These tools generate interactive HTML reports with scatter plots, box plots, and sortable tables to evaluate docking results.

For detailed information about CAPRI metric calculations, see [CAPRI Evaluation](#4.5.1). For clustering algorithms, see [Clustering](#4.5.2). For interface residue analysis, see [Alanine Scanning](#4.5.3).

---

## Selection Modules

HADDOCK3 provides two modules for selecting subsets of models to pass to subsequent workflow steps.

### seletop Module

The `seletop` module performs simple selection of the top N models based on score. It retrieves models from the previous step, sorts them by their `score` attribute, and selects the specified number.

**Module**: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/seletop/__init__.py:1-66]()

**Key Parameters**:
- `select`: Number of models to select (default: 200)

**Implementation Details**:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "seletop Module Workflow"
        Input["previous_io.output<br/>List of PDBFile objects"]
        Filter["Filter PDBFile objects<br/>by file_type == Format.PDB"]
        Sort["Sort by PDBFile.score<br/>ascending order"]
        Select["Select first params['select']<br/>models"]
        Output["output_models<br/>Selected subset"]
        
        Input --> Filter
        Filter --> Sort
        Sort --> Select
        Select --> Output
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Structures"
        PDBFile["PDBFile<br/>- file_name<br/>- score<br/>- file_type"]
    end
    
    Select -.references.- PDBFile
```

**Sources**: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/seletop/__init__.py:40-65]()

---

### seletopclusts Module

The `seletopclusts` module provides more sophisticated selection by choosing the top N models from the top M clusters. This maintains diversity by ensuring representation from multiple clusters rather than taking all models from the best cluster.

**Module**: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/seletopclusts/__init__.py:1-90]()

**Key Parameters**:
- `top_clusters`: Number of clusters to consider
- `top_models`: Number of models to select per cluster
- `sortby`: Metric to use for ranking (default: "score")

**Selection Algorithm**:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "seletopclusts Workflow"
        Input["previous_io.retrieve_models()"]
        ValidateCluster["Check for cluster info<br/>PDBFile.clt_rank must exist"]
        SelectFunc["select_top_clusts_models()"]
        GroupClusters["Group models by cluster_id"]
        RankClusters["Sort clusters by mean score"]
        SelectTopClust["Select top_clusters clusters"]
        SelectModels["From each cluster select<br/>top_models models by sortby"]
        Write["write_selected_models()<br/>Rename and copy to current dir"]
        Output["output_models"]
        
        Input --> ValidateCluster
        ValidateCluster --> SelectFunc
        SelectFunc --> GroupClusters
        GroupClusters --> RankClusters
        RankClusters --> SelectTopClust
        SelectTopClust --> SelectModels
        SelectModels --> Write
        Write --> Output
    end
```

**Sources**: [src/haddock/modules/analysis/seletopclusts/__init__.py:46-89](), [src/haddock/modules/analysis/seletopclusts/seletopclusts.py]()

---

## Visualization Library Architecture

The visualization system is implemented in `libplots.py` and provides interactive plotting capabilities using Plotly. All plots are generated as HTML files with embedded JavaScript for interactivity.

### Core Plotting Functions

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "libplots.py Core Components"
        ReadCapri["read_capri_table()<br/>Load TSV files"]
        ScatterHandler["scatter_plot_handler()<br/>Generate scatter plots"]
        BoxHandler["box_plot_handler()<br/>Generate box plots"]
        TableHandler["clt_table_handler()<br/>Generate data tables"]
        ReportGen["report_generator()<br/>Combine into HTML report"]
        
        ReadCapri --> ScatterHandler
        ReadCapri --> BoxHandler
        ReadCapri --> TableHandler
        
        ScatterHandler --> ReportGen
        BoxHandler --> ReportGen
        TableHandler --> ReportGen
    end
    
    subgraph "Plot Generation Functions"
        ScatterPlotly["scatter_plot_plotly()<br/>Create plotly.graph_objects.Figure"]
        BoxPlotly["box_plot_plotly()<br/>Create plotly.graph_objects.Figure"]
        CreateHTML["create_html()<br/>Convert to HTML string"]
        
        ScatterHandler --> ScatterPlotly
        BoxHandler --> BoxPlotly
        
        ScatterPlotly --> CreateHTML
        BoxPlotly --> CreateHTML
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Files"
        HTMLPlots["Individual HTML files<br/>irmsd_score.html<br/>score_clt.html<br/>etc."]
        Report["report.html<br/>Consolidated report"]
        
        CreateHTML --> HTMLPlots
        ReportGen --> Report
    end
```

**Sources**: [src/haddock/libs/libplots.py:1-160](), [src/haddock/libs/libplots.py:400-647]()

---

### Scatter Plot Generation

Scatter plots visualize relationships between CAPRI metrics (i-RMSD, l-RMSD, FNAT, DockQ) and energy terms (score, VdW, elec, desolv, AIR).

**Key Variables and Functions**:

| Component | Location | Description |
|-----------|----------|-------------|
| `SCATTER_PAIRS` | [src/haddock/libs/libplots.py:31-57]() | List of 25 metric pairs to plot |
| `AXIS_NAMES` | [src/haddock/libs/libplots.py:77-89]() | Human-readable axis labels |
| `scatter_plot_handler()` | [src/haddock/libs/libplots.py:594-646]() | Orchestrates scatter plot generation |
| `scatter_plot_plotly()` | [src/haddock/libs/libplots.py:401-563]() | Creates individual scatter plot Figure |
| `scatter_plot_data()` | [src/haddock/libs/libplots.py:566-591]() | Prepares data by grouping clusters |

**Scatter Plot Features**:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Scatter Plot Elements"
        Points["Individual Model Points<br/>Colored by cluster"]
        Centroids["Cluster Centroids<br/>Square markers with error bars"]
        Hover["Hover Text<br/>Model name, score, rank"]
        Legend["Legend<br/>Cluster names"]
        Other["'Other' Cluster<br/>White circles with border"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Calculation"
        Top4["Top 4 models per cluster"]
        Mean["Calculate mean(x), mean(y)"]
        Std["Calculate std(x), std(y)"]
        
        Top4 --> Mean
        Top4 --> Std
        Mean --> Centroids
        Std --> Centroids
    end
```

Each scatter plot includes:
- Individual model points colored by cluster membership
- Cluster centroids as larger square markers with error bars (mean ± std of top 4 models)
- Interactive hover text showing model path, score, and CAPRI rank
- Models not in top clusters grouped into "Other" category

**Sources**: [src/haddock/libs/libplots.py:401-563]()
